science.title: The combination of yeast cell wall and Heyndrickxia coagulans SANK70258 maximized butyrate production in an in vitro gut model
science.description: In recent years, increasing attention has been paid to synbiotic formulations comprising prebiotics and probiotics. Yeast cell walls (YCW) constitute a well-known industrial material with partial prebiotic effects. Its potential as a synbiotic agent that can add value to functional food has not been evaluated. In this exploratory research, we aimed to test if the probiotic bacterium Heyndrickxia coagulans SANK70258 (COA), when combined with YCW, could modulate the gut microbial community and increase the concentration of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), particularly butyric acid. To this purpose, we performed an in vitro fermentation assay using fecal samples from healthy participants. Non-supplemented control samples and YCW, COA, and SYN (COA + YCW) treatments were included. SCFAs production and microbial composition were analyzed at 48 h. Butyrate concentration was highest in the SYN treatment, possibly in association with the availability of fermentable YCW-derived carbon sources. YCW-derived substrates might support the proliferation of Bacteroides, which may in turn be associated with COA-mediated promotion of butyrate-producing bacteria such as Faecalibacterium. COA might additionally suppress some Bacteroides-competitive taxa, further facilitating Bacteroides proliferation. Thus, combining YCW with COA in a SYN formulation could improve butyrate production and promote a healthier gut environment.

science.title: Prevalence and characteristics of self-reported sports-related injuries among university students: a cross-sectional study
science.description: Sports-related injuries among recreationally active university students remain incompletely described. This study estimated past-year injury prevalence, described lifetime injury-history characteristics, and explored associations between past-year injury occurrence and participant characteristics. This cross-sectional survey collected 394 responses at a Saudi university during January–December 2025. After excluding three nonconsenting respondents and 108 consenting nonparticipants, 283 active students were analysed. Exploratory logistic regression included sex, age group, body mass index category, participation frequency, perceived training intensity, and chronic disease. Overall, 157 students reported past-year injury (55.5%; 95% confidence interval [CI] 49.7–61.2%), and 178 reported lifetime injury. Among 281 complete cases, male respondents had higher adjusted odds of past-year injury reporting than female respondents (adjusted odds ratio 2.48; 95% CI 1.32–4.65; p = 0.005), with similar estimates across sensitivity analyses. No association with chronic disease was detected. Among lifetime injury reporters, 65.7% selected contact sports and 36.5% reported visiting a doctor or physiotherapist. Self-reported sports-related injuries were common among physically active students in this single-university convenience sample. The findings provide exploratory, descriptive evidence and should not be interpreted as sport-specific injury rates or causal effects because exposure time was not measured and injuries were not clinically verified.

science.title: Anthropic's Claude Science creates the first complete ultraviolet map of the sky
science.description: Astrophysicist Brice Ménard of Johns Hopkins University used Anthropic's Claude Science to map the entire sky in ultraviolet light for the first time. AI agents downloaded data from multiple space missions, calibrated it, and filled in gaps using inpainting. Predictions averaged about ten percent deviation from actual measurements. Ménard sees the project as an example of research that simply wouldn't have gotten done without AI.
